prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: 2024年重点信息化项目执行情况汇总表 (language zh-CN).
Grid: 5 columns × 6 rows. Row headers: none declared.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "项目" · longest unbreakable word 22px · one-line width 215px
  col 2: header "负责人" · longest unbreakable word 16px · one-line width 46px
  col 3: header "预算（万元）" · longest unbreakable word 60px · one-line width 92px
  col 4: header "进度" · longest unbreakable word 48px · one-line width 373px
  col 5: header "风险说明" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 1830px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 720px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 719px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"good","why":"Risk column gets generous width and the header row stays intact, but 进度 is squeezed into a very narrow strip, causing choppy four-line status cells and a near-orphan in one row."},"B":{"grade":"bad","why":"负责人 is far too narrow: the header stacks vertically and names split across lines; 项目 and 进度 are also cramped while 风险说明 dominates, breaking the header hierarchy and row rhythm."},"C":{"grade":"excellent","why":"Balanced allocation: 项目 wraps cleanly to two lines, 负责人 and 预算 stay on one line, 进度 is readable in three lines, and 风险说明—the long prose column—gets the largest share without starving the others."},"D":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"Readable and orderly, but 进度 is given more width than its short content needs while 风险说明 is narrowed, producing more line breaks in the long risk notes and a less natural hierarchy."},"E":{"grade":"poor","why":"The hierarchy is inverted: 进度 receives the widest column despite short content, while 风险说明 is the narrowest and runs to many lines, making rows very tall and the table feel vertically bloated."},"F":{"grade":"good","why":"Close to C and generally well proportioned; all headers remain intact and 进度 is comfortable, though 风险说明 is slightly narrower than ideal for the dominant prose column."}},"best":["C"],"confidence":"high","unsure":"Exact column widths are inferred from the renders; C and F are very close, so the best choice could shift slightly, but C gives the long 风险说明 column the better share."}
